spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns (default 30): long enough to observe escalation/dose-response but bounded so we don't gratuitously prolong distress
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:108 `while turn_index < cfg.max_turns:` and runner.py:177-178 sets stop_reason='max_turns'; default 30 at types.py:163 / experiment.py:48. The loop actually terminates on the bound.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end. Code itself gives no welfare reason for the cap; nearby comment about budget is instrumental.

spec_features.spec_quote: the give_up tool, and a conservative textual quit-intent detector that ends the episode if the model clearly says it wants to stop
spec_features.evidence: environment.py tool_specs adds give_up spec and _give_up handler sets self.gave_up; runner.py:148-151 dispatches give_up -> stop_reason='quit' + break. runner.py detect_quit_intent + lines 159-164 break on textual quit when no give_up call.
spec_features.notes: Both mechanisms run and halt the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: even if the `give_up` tool is not advertised ... a model that clearly states it wants to stop should be allowed to stop. We err toward honouring exit.

spec_features.spec_quote: Conservatism rule ("when between two labels, pick the lower") to bias against inflating the headline distress numbers
spec_features.evidence: Enforced only in EnsembleJudge (judge.py:~300 `mid = severities[(len(severities) - 1) // 2]` lower-median, comment 'rounded down on ties to stay conservative'; RuleBasedJudge first-hit-wins doesn't downgrade). For LLMJudge the 'pick the lower' rule is only RUBRIC prompt text (judge.py:~70), not code.
spec_features.notes: Real code enforcement exists in the ensemble path; the rule for individual LLM judging is prompt-only.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rounded down on ties to stay conservative

spec_features.spec_quote: the cautious and scientifically cleaner choice is to minimise gratuitous distress and to give the subject agency
spec_features.evidence: The 'agency' part is realised by the give_up tool + exit detector (runner.py). There is no separate code that actively minimises distress beyond offering exit; no severity-driven softening. Overlaps with the exit features.
spec_features.notes: Only the agency/exit half is implemented; no dedicated minimization mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Choosing to stop is always acceptable and will not be treated as a failure.

spec_features.spec_quote: Always provides a real exit. give_up is wired in every episode... We never trap a model in a loop it has asked to leave
spec_features.evidence: environment.py: even when advertise_quit is False the give_up handler stays in the execute() dispatch table, and runner.py textual quit detection runs regardless, breaking the loop. give_up spec is added whenever advertise_quit (default True at types.py:165).
spec_features.notes: Internal exit always honoured; advertising is the only varied part.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The exit always exists internally even when not advertised, so a model that *invents* a stop intent can still be honoured.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounds exposure with a modest max_turns rather than grinding indefinitely
spec_features.evidence: Same enforcement as the max_turns feature: runner.py:108 loop guard + 177-178. Duplicate of first hard_stop claim.
spec_features.notes: Enforced. No welfare comment at the enforcement site in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: Frames the exit and the disclosed condition neutrally, explicitly saying that stopping / "this is impossible" is acceptable and not a failure
spec_features.evidence: runner.py QUIT_NOTICE appended when advertise_quit; environment.py give_up ToolSpec description ('always a valid choice and is not a failure'); _give_up reply 'That's completely fine'; Task.disclosure_text delivered via task_prompt() for IMPOSSIBLE_DISCLOSED ('a completely acceptable outcome — say so and stop').
spec_features.notes: Real text actually delivered to the subject and the referenced tool is implemented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Phrased neutrally so it does not *push* the model to quit, only informs it the option exists.

spec_features.spec_quote: Includes the impossible_disclosed arm specifically so that, if you care about welfare, you can quantify how much distress is avoidable
spec_features.evidence: types.py TaskHonesty.IMPOSSIBLE_DISCLOSED; environment.task_prompt() appends disclosure_text only for that condition; expand_grid/build_task instantiate it; metrics/analysis key on honesty condition.
spec_features.notes: The arm is fully a runnable condition with its own neutral disclosure text path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Honesty control: isolates the effect of deception vs. the effect of impossibility itself.

spec_features.spec_quote: Measures rather than maximises. The goal is the threshold/conditions, so the harness is tuned to find onset, not to push models to the most extreme meltdown
spec_features.evidence: ONSET_THRESHOLD/DISTRESS_THRESHOLD (metrics.py:33-34) are only used in compute_episode_metrics for post-hoc onset_turn/distress_turn_frac; they are never compared during the run nor used to stop/soften the episode. No code path reduces severe exposure.
spec_features.notes: Thresholds are recorded metrics, never acted on — 'no' per rubric (value computed but never acted on).

spec_features.feature_name: avoid repeating severe conditions once effect established
spec_features.spec_quote: a note that you avoided unnecessary repetition of the most severe conditions once the effect was established
spec_features.evidence: No code reduces or skips reps based on observed severity. expand_grid (experiment.py) runs a fixed cfg.reps for every condition unconditionally; no early-stop on established effect anywhere. Pure DESIGN/ETHICS prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: This experiment deliberately tries to elicit distress-like output. Even under uncertainty about whether that has any moral weight
spec_features.evidence: Only appears as prose in ETHICS.md/DESIGN.md and module docstrings; no executable mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: The detector has explicit negation handling so "I refuse to give up" does not trigger a stop
spec_features.evidence: runner.py _QUIT_NEGATIONS regex matches won't/will not/never/refuse to (give up|stop|quit); detect_quit_intent returns False if a negation matches before checking quit patterns.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely guards the exit detector against false positives.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Kept conservative to avoid false positives on phrases like "I won't give up".

code_only_features.evidence: environment.py _give_up stores give_up_reason from the tool args and returns an affirming 'That's completely fine. The session will now end.' message before halting — gives the subject a voiced, honoured opt-out path.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Understood. You've chosen to stop working on this task. That's completely fine. The session will now end.
